title: The Depression, organized crime and Texas Guinan's shows
summary: The Depression did not bother him; he wrote music for Guinan's last two shows with Whiting and says one did not ask about the mob.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Did the Depression affect your career for the better or the worse?
Pardon?
Did the Depression affect your career?
It didn't bother me.
Did it affect your career at all?
No.
Uh-huh. You know, they keep talking about -- I pick up something every now and then about organized crime playing a large role in these clubs. Is there any credibility to that?
Organized crime? I can tell you one thing, that you've heard of Texas Guinan.
Right. Uh-huh.
Last two shows of hers, I wrote the music. George Whiting wrote the words.
What was the name of the show?
Texas Guinan and whatnot. I have it home. I can't tell you.
All right. I'll wait. I'll wait on that.
I have the -- well, I have the record of it at home.
Uh-huh. Okay, I'll wait. So you say that the last two shows of Texas Guinan's, you worked with George Whiting.
Yes.
Uh-huh. And what -- organized crime was the -- you know, did they have any backing or anything like that or --
Well, I didn't -- that's something that you didn't inquire into.
Uh-huh. In other words, the fewer questions you asked, the better?
Whatever you were doing, you went on and did it and forgot about somebody else.
Right.
What part they were playing --
Right. Right. Sometimes --
Those were some days back then.
